That's a great question, but it requires some crucial clarification: **There has never been a French submarine *class* officially named "Narval-class."** The name "Narval" (French for "Narwhal") has been used for *individual French submarines*, spanning different eras and technologies, but never for an entire class designation.

This confusion is very common! People often hear "French submarine Narval" and assume "Narval-class" exists. Let's break down everything related to the name "Narval" in the French Navy (Marine Nationale), covering historical vessels and the *planned* future submarine:

## 1. The Original & Revolutionary: *Narval* (Q4) - 1899
*   **Significance:** This is the **most famous and historically important** vessel bearing the name. Designed by **Gaston Romazzotti**, it wasn't just *a* submarine; it pioneered a fundamental design principle still used today.
*   **Revolutionary Innovation:** It was the **world's first operational submarine with a double hull.** The inner pressure hull maintained structural integrity at depth, while the outer hydrodynamic hull improved surface seakeeping and stability. This concept became standard for almost all subsequent submarines globally.
*   **Technical Specifications (Q4):**
    *   **Displacement:** 243 tons surfaced, 315 tons submerged
    *   **Length:** 45.88 m (150 ft 6 in)
    *   **Beam:** 3.75 m (12 ft 4 in)
    *   **Draught:** 3.3 m (10 ft 10 in)
    *   **Propulsion:**
        *   *Surface:* 1 x 400 hp Daimler gasoline engine
        *   *Submerged:* 1 x 180 hp electric motor
    *   **Speed:** 8.5 knots (surfaced), 6.5 knots (submerged)
    *   **Range:** ~700 nmi @ 6.5 kts surfaced
    *   **Armament:** 1 x 450 mm (17.7 in) bow torpedo tube, 2 torpedoes
    *   **Crew:** 2 officers, 11 enlisted
*   **Service:** Commissioned in 1899. Served actively until 1910, then used as a training hulk until 1920. Proved the viability of the double-hull concept, influencing submarine design worldwide (including German WWI U-boats).
*   **Why it wasn't a "Class":** While revolutionary, its design was quickly superseded. Only **one** *Narval* (Q4) was built to this specific Romazzotti design. Later French classes (like the *Emeraude*-class) adopted the double-hull principle but were distinct designs.

## 2. World War II Era: *Narval* (NN5) - 1925
*   **Significance:** A large, ocean-going "cruiser submarine" designed for long-range operations, particularly in the Far East to protect French colonies. Represented the peak of French interwar submarine design.
*   **Class:** She was the **lead boat of the *Requin*-class** (sometimes called the *Narval*-class *unofficially* due to her prominence, but *never officially* by the French Navy). 15 boats were built in this class.
*   **Technical Specifications (Requin-class - NN5):**
    *   **Displacement:** 1,150 tons surfaced, 1,425 tons submerged
    *   **Length:** 80 m (262 ft 6 in)
    *   **Beam:** 7.1 m (23 ft 4 in)
    *   **Draught:** 4.9 m (16 ft 1 in)
    *   **Propulsion:**
        *   *Surface:* 2 x 2,200 hp diesels
        *   *Submerged:* 2 x 850 hp electric motors
    *   **Speed:** 18.5 knots (surfaced), 9 knots (submerged)
    *   **Range:** ~9,000 nmi @ 11 kts surfaced
    *   **Armament:**
        *   1 x 100mm deck gun
        *   1 x 13.2mm AA machine gun
        *   11 x 550mm torpedo tubes (6 bow, 4 stern, 1 external stern): 18 torpedoes
    *   **Crew:** 5 officers, 59 enlisted
*   **Service:** Commissioned 1927. Initially served in the Mediterranean and French Indochina. At the outbreak of WWII, she was in French Indochina. Remained loyal to Vichy France after 1940. Scuttled by her crew on September 9, 1940, in Saigon (now Ho Chi Minh City) to avoid capture by the Japanese during their occupation of French Indochina. **She was *not* the lead of a class named "Narval."**

## 3. The Modern & Future: *Narval* (S642) - Planned (Suffren/Barracuda-class)
*   **Significance:** This is **why the confusion about a "Narval-class" is so prevalent today.** The French Navy announced in **2023** that the **seventh and final submarine** of the new **Suffren-class** (Barracuda program) nuclear attack submarines (SSNs) will be named ***Narval***.
*   **Class:** This submarine **will be part of the *Suffren*-class** (also known as the *Barracuda*-class). The class is named after its lead boat, *Suffren* (Q284), commissioned in 2020. There is **no "Narval-class"**; *Narval* will be the name of **one specific boat within the Suffren-class**.
*   **Current Status:**
    *   **Planned Name:** *Narval* (S642 - following the historical designation scheme for SSNs).
    *   **Program:** Barracuda (Suffren-class SSN).
    *   **Role:** Nuclear-powered fast attack submarine (SSN) for power projection, anti-submarine warfare (ASW), anti-surface warfare (ASuW), intelligence gathering, special forces delivery, and strategic deterrence support (though not a ballistic missile sub).
*   **Expected Specifications (aligned with Suffren-class):**
    *   **Displacement:** ~5,300 tons
    *   **Length:** 97 m (318 ft)
    *   **Beam:** 8.8 m (29 ft)
    *   **Propulsion:** K15 pressurized water nuclear reactor (same as *Charles de Gaulle* carrier) driving a single pump-jet, 1 x emergency diesel.
    *   **Speed:** >25 knots (exact classified)
    *   **Range:** Limited only by food supplies and maintenance (decades of operation on one fuel load).
    *   **Armament:**
        *   4 x 533mm torpedo tubes
        *   F21 Artemis heavyweight torpedoes
        *   Naval Cruise Missiles (MdCN - ~1,000 km range)
        *   Sub-Harpoon anti-ship missiles
        *   Capacity for mines
    *   **Crew:** ~60
    *   **Sensors:** Advanced SYCOBS combat system, Thales sonars (including retractable towed array), sophisticated optronics.
    *   **Stealth:** Extremely quiet design, pump-jet propulsion, advanced acoustic damping.
*   **Timeline:**
    *   **Announced:** Name confirmed by French Minister of the Armed Forces Sébastien Lecornu on July 1, 2023.
    *   **Construction:** Expected to begin around 2025-2026 at Naval Group's Cherbourg shipyard.
    *   **Commissioning:** Likely in the **late 2020s or early 2030s** (exact date depends on construction pace and priorities). *Suffren* (1st), *Duguay-Trouin* (2nd), *Tourville* (3rd), *De Grasse* (4th), *Dupetit-Thouars* (5th), and *Duquesne* (6th) are all under construction or commissioned. *Narval* is #7.
*   **Why the Name?** The French Navy deliberately chose *Narval* to honor the **pioneering legacy of the 1899 submarine**, symbolizing a return to the cutting-edge innovation and ambition embodied by Romazzotti's original design, now realized with 21st-century nuclear technology.

## Critical Clarifications & Common Confusions

1.  **"Narval-class" DOES NOT EXIST:** Neither historically nor currently. Submarines have *classes* (e.g., *Requin*-class, *Suffren*-class) and *individual names* (*Narval*, *Suffren*). The class name comes from the *first boat commissioned* in that design series.
2.  **Soviet/Russian *Narval* (1957):** This was a **Project 615 (Quebec-class) diesel-electric submarine** of the **Soviet Navy**. It has **no connection whatsoever** to the French Navy or its naming traditions. This sometimes causes confusion in non-French sources.
3.  **Modern Suffren-class is NOT called "Narval-class":** Only the 7th boat will carry the name *Narval*. The class remains the *Suffren*-class. Calling it "Narval-class" before the boat is even built is incorrect and not used by the French Navy.
4.  **Historical Precedent:** The French Navy has a tradition of reusing prestigious names. *Narval* (1899) was named after the Arctic whale. *Narval* (1925) reused that historic name. The upcoming SSN continues that tradition.

## Summary

*   **1899 *Narval* (Q4):** A single, revolutionary **double-hull pioneer** (not a class leader).
*   **1925 *Narval* (NN5):** The **lead boat of the *Requin*-class** (not a "Narval-class").
*   **Planned *Narval* (S642):** The **7th and final boat** of the **Suffren-class (Barracuda program)** nuclear attack submarines, named to honor the 1899 pioneer. Expected commissioning late 2020s/early 2030s.
*   **NO "Narval-class" exists or has ever existed in the French Navy.**

The name *Narval* carries immense historical weight in French submarine development due to the 1899 boat's groundbreaking design. The upcoming Suffren-class SSN bearing the name is a deliberate tribute to that legacy, but it firmly belongs to the *Suffren*-class, not a new "Narval-class." If you hear "French Narval-class submarine," it almost certainly refers to a misunderstanding of either the historical *Requin*-class boat or, more likely today, the planned Suffren-class boat named *Narval*.
